subject: gunblade
pitch:
Category: Weapon.
Subject: gunblade.
Style: Final Fantasy.

requests.what: Lion-head emblem engraved on the blade's left face near the ricasso, as a small raised relief in GOLD with GOLD_DARK outline, plus two tiny rivets either side. Mirror a plainer version on the right face.
Ornate filigree on both gold wing guards: layered feather-like ridges in GOLD_DARK and GOLD_LIGHT-ish trims, small studs along the edges.
Engraved rings, tiny screws and a gold bezel around each of the six chamber holes on both faces of the revolver cylinder; chamber rims in GOLD, tiny CRYSTAL lights between chambers.
Muzzle brake at the barrel tip: ventilated slots, a gold crown ring and a small front sight blade, plus a fine ring of grooves under it.
Detailed hammer spur with knurling, a trigger with a small pivot pin and a spring behind it, in GUNMETAL_DARK and STEEL.
Crossed leather wrapping bands with gold studs at the top and bottom of the grip and a small red cloth tassel strap wrapped around the middle.

A short silver chain hanging from the pommel ring ending in a lion-head pendant charm (GOLD) with a tiny CRYSTAL eye. Chain hangs but must not go below y = 0 more than 2 cm; keep it coiled beside the pommel.
Decorative notches and small gold clamps joining the barrel to the blade spine, three of them evenly along the barrel with bolts.
Fine etched steel look on both blade faces: brushed streaks along the length, a lighter bevel near the edge, faint blue-tinted rune line down the fuller in CRYSTAL, and subtle battle scratches.
Dark stitched leather in LEATHER and LEATHER_LIGHT with diagonal wrap seams and worn highlights.
Polished silver-steel with gold inlaid lines and slight bluing near chambers, matching the STEEL and GOLD palette.

calls.reasoning:
I'm designing a Final Fantasy-style gunblade module, static with no joints, around 1.3m long, standing upright with the pommel resting at floor level and the blade facing forward.

I'm laying out the pieces vertically: a gold pommel at the base, a leather-wrapped grip above it, a revolver-style cylinder with chambers and a trigger guard partway up, and a tapered blade extending to the top, defining the blade's cross-section with a spine and cutting edge.

Now I'm detailing the blade further—adding a barrel along the spine with a muzzle, a beveled edge strip, fuller grooves, a gold ricasso plate, and a swept tip—then thinking about adding a lion emblem and gold wing-shaped guard plates flanking the cylinder.

I also want a hanging chain with a glowing blue gem and matching glow on the chambers, pulling in a glow kit. I'm sketching helper functions for boxes and cylinders along arbitrary axes, then working out the blade's extruded outline and positioning the spine barrel relative to it.

Now I'm planning the additional detail parts: an emblem on the blade, grip wrap, hammer details, cylinder engraving, muzzle, pommel charm, guard filigree, plus texture layers for edge etching, blade runes, and grip leather, naming parts like "bladeSide," "grip," and "cylinder" so textures can target them.

I'm working out placement for the trigger guard as a half-torus oriented in the YZ plane near the front, a small trigger box, and an angled hammer box behind the cylinder. For the grip, I'm adding gold torus rings as wraps along its length, with a rounded pommel featuring a glowing blue gem at the base.

Now I'm shaping the pommel using a lathed profile that tapers out then back in near the bottom, and sizing the receiver as a dark navy box positioned above it. I'm also placing the revolver cylinder as a short silver-and-gold rimmed drum with a ring of small chamber holes on each face, sitting just below where the blade base begins.

Now I'm building the guard pieces as angular gold wedge plates swept forward and down on either side of the hilt, plus a smaller back guard, while keeping the overall height around 1.2 units with the pommel resting at the ground plane. I'm computing the chamber hole positions around the cylinder face using sine and cosine to space them evenly in a ring.

Still writing geometry...
